# Two-group random-intercept design: sample size for 90% power
# Analyzing participant-level averages with two-sided t-test

# Study parameters
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1  # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
delta <- 0.45  # mean group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.90
allocation_ratio <- 1  # equal groups

# Step 1: Variance of participant-level average
# Var(avg) = sigma_marginal^2 * [rho + (1-rho)/m]
var_avg <- sigma_marginal^2 * (rho + (1 - rho) / m)
sd_avg <- sqrt(var_avg)

cat("Participant-level average variance component:\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ_i) = σ²_marginal × [ρ + (1-ρ)/m]\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ_i) = 1² × [0.4 + 0.6/4]\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ_i) =", var_avg, "\n")
cat("SD(Ȳ_i) =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Effective standardized effect size for participant averages
# d = δ / SD(avg) where δ is the true difference
effect_size <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d on participant averages):\n")
cat("d = Δ / SD(Ȳ_i) = 0.45 /", sd_avg, "=", effect_size, "\n\n")

# Step 3: Sample size calculation via inversion for two-sided t-test
# For balanced design (n per group), the t-test has df = 2n - 2
# noncentrality parameter: λ = d * sqrt(n/2) for equal-n design
# Power = P(|t| > t_crit) under H1 with df = 2n-2 and λ

library(stats)

# Function to compute power at sample size n
power_at_n <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha, df_formula = function(n) 2*n - 2) {
  df <- df_formula(n_per_group)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)  # two-sided critical value
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # noncentrality parameter for balanced design
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n achieving target power
power_vec <- numeric(100)
n_vec <- 1:100

for (n in n_vec) {
  power_vec[n] <- power_at_n(n, effect_size, alpha)
}

# Find first n where power >= 0.90
min_n_exact <- min(which(power_vec >= target_power))
power_at_min_n <- power_vec[min_n_exact]

cat("Sample size search (two-sided pooled t-test):\n")
cat("Effect size d =", effect_size, "\n")
cat("Target power =", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level α =", alpha, "\n\n")

# Show convergence
indices_near <- max(1, min_n_exact - 2):min(length(power_vec), min_n_exact + 2)
comparison <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = indices_near,
  power = power_vec[indices_near]
)
print(comparison)

cat("\nMinimum participants per group (integer): ", min_n_exact, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n_exact, ":", power_at_min_n, "\n\n")

# Verify previous value
if (min_n_exact > 1) {
  power_at_prev <- power_vec[min_n_exact - 1]
  cat("Power at n =", min_n_exact - 1, ":", power_at_prev, "\n")
}

# Summary output
cat("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group: ", min_n_exact, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", round(power_at_min_n, 6), "\n")

# Export as POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n_exact,
  unit = "participants_per_group"
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = result),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
), "\n")

# Under random-intercept: Y_ij = b_i + epsilon_ij
# where b_i ~ N(0, sigma_b^2) and epsilon_ij ~ N(0, sigma_e^2)
# marginal variance = sigma_b^2 + sigma_e^2 = sigma_marginal^2
# ICC = sigma_b^2 / (sigma_b^2 + sigma_e^2)
# So: sigma_b^2 = rho * sigma_marginal^2, sigma_e^2 = (1-rho) * sigma_marginal^2

sigma_b_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_e_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Random-intercept variance decomposition:\n")
cat("  sigma_b² =", sigma_b_sq, "(between-participant variance)\n")
cat("  sigma_e² =", sigma_e_sq, "(within-participant variance)\n")
cat("  Marginal variance = sigma_b² + sigma_e² =", sigma_b_sq + sigma_e_sq, "\n\n")

# Variance of participant average Ȳ_i = (1/m) Σ_j Y_ij
# Var(Ȳ_i) = Var(b_i) + Var((1/m) Σ_j epsilon_ij)
#          = sigma_b^2 + sigma_e^2/m
#          = rho*sigma_marg^2 + (1-rho)*sigma_marg^2/m

sd_avg_check <- sqrt(var_avg_check)

cat("Variance of participant-level average:\n")
cat("  Var(Ȳ_i) = sigma_b² + sigma_e²/m\n")

simulate_study <- function(n_per_group, m, sigma_b_sq, sigma_e_sq, delta, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  
  # Generate random intercepts for each participant
  # Group 1 (n participants)
  b_1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_b_sq))
  # Group 2 (n participants)
  b_2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_b_sq))
  
  # Generate observations (constant mean difference delta)
  # Group 1: mean = 0, Group 2: mean = delta
  
  # Group 1 participant averages
  Y_1 <- numeric(n_per_group)
  for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
    eps_i <- rnorm(m, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_e_sq))
    Y_1[i] <- b_1[i] + mean(eps_i)  # average of 4 obs for participant i
  }
  
  # Group 2 participant averages
  Y_2 <- numeric(n_per_group)
  for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
    eps_i <- rnorm(m, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_e_sq))
    Y_2[i] <- delta + b_2[i] + mean(eps_i)  # add delta for group 2
  }
  
  # Two-sided pooled t-test on participant averages
  t_result <- t.test(Y_1, Y_2, var.equal = TRUE)
  
  # Return TRUE if H0 is rejected (two-sided, alpha = 0.05)
  return(t_result$p.value < alpha)
}

# Two-group random-intercept design: sample size for 90% power
# Analyzing participant-level averages with two-sided t-test

# Study parameters
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1  # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
delta <- 0.45  # mean group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.90
allocation_ratio <- 1  # equal groups

# Step 1: Variance of participant-level average
# Var(avg) = sigma_marginal^2 * [rho + (1-rho)/m]
var_avg <- sigma_marginal^2 * (rho + (1 - rho) / m)
sd_avg <- sqrt(var_avg)

cat("Participant-level average variance component:\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ_i) = σ²_marginal × [ρ + (1-ρ)/m]\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ_i) = 1² × [0.4 + 0.6/4]\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ_i) =", var_avg, "\n")
cat("SD(Ȳ_i) =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Effective standardized effect size for participant averages
# d = δ / SD(avg) where δ is the true difference
effect_size <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d on participant averages):\n")
cat("d = Δ / SD(Ȳ_i) = 0.45 /", sd_avg, "=", effect_size, "\n\n")

# Step 3: Sample size calculation via inversion for two-sided t-test
# For balanced design (n per group), the t-test has df = 2n - 2
# noncentrality parameter: λ = d * sqrt(n/2) for equal-n design
# Power = P(|t| > t_crit) under H1 with df = 2n-2 and λ

library(stats)

# Function to compute power at sample size n
power_at_n <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha, df_formula = function(n) 2*n - 2) {
  df <- df_formula(n_per_group)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)  # two-sided critical value
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # noncentrality parameter for balanced design
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n achieving target power
power_vec <- numeric(100)
n_vec <- 1:100

for (n in n_vec) {
  power_vec[n] <- power_at_n(n, effect_size, alpha)
}

# Find first n where power >= 0.90
min_n_exact <- min(which(power_vec >= target_power))
power_at_min_n <- power_vec[min_n_exact]

cat("Sample size search (two-sided pooled t-test):\n")
cat("Effect size d =", effect_size, "\n")
cat("Target power =", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level α =", alpha, "\n\n")

  n_per_group = indices_near,
  power = power_vec[indices_near]
)

cat("\nMinimum participants per group (integer): ", min_n_exact, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n_exact, ":", power_at_min_n, "\n\n")

# Verify previous value

  power_at_prev <- power_vec[min_n_exact - 1]
  cat("Power at n =", min_n_exact - 1, ":", power_at_prev, "\n")
}

# Summary output
cat("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group: ", min_n_exact, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", round(power_at_min_n, 6), "\n")

# Export as POWER_AGENT_RESULT

)

  list(results = result),

# Independent verification using both analytical and simulation-based approaches

set.seed(42)

# Study parameters (from original request)
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4
delta <- 0.45
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90

# ============================================================================
# METHOD 1: Analytical approach (verify candidate's method)
# ============================================================================

cat("METHOD 1: ANALYTICAL POWER CALCULATION\n")
cat("=======================================\n\n")

# Step 1: Compute variance of participant average
# Under random-intercept: Y_ij = b_i + epsilon_ij
# where b_i ~ N(0, sigma_b^2) and epsilon_ij ~ N(0, sigma_e^2)
# marginal variance = sigma_b^2 + sigma_e^2 = sigma_marginal^2
# ICC = sigma_b^2 / (sigma_b^2 + sigma_e^2)
# So: sigma_b^2 = rho * sigma_marginal^2, sigma_e^2 = (1-rho) * sigma_marginal^2

sigma_b_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_e_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Random-intercept variance decomposition:\n")
cat("  sigma_b² =", sigma_b_sq, "(between-participant variance)\n")
cat("  sigma_e² =", sigma_e_sq, "(within-participant variance)\n")
cat("  Marginal variance = sigma_b² + sigma_e² =", sigma_b_sq + sigma_e_sq, "\n\n")

# Variance of participant average Ȳ_i = (1/m) Σ_j Y_ij
# Var(Ȳ_i) = Var(b_i) + Var((1/m) Σ_j epsilon_ij)
#          = sigma_b^2 + sigma_e^2/m
#          = rho*sigma_marg^2 + (1-rho)*sigma_marg^2/m

var_avg_check <- sigma_b_sq + sigma_e_sq / m
sd_avg_check <- sqrt(var_avg_check)

cat("Variance of participant-level average:\n")
cat("  Var(Ȳ_i) = sigma_b² + sigma_e²/m\n")
cat("  Var(Ȳ_i) =", sigma_b_sq, "+", sigma_e_sq/m, "=", var_avg_check, "\n")
cat("  SD(Ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_check, "\n\n")

# Alternative formula verification
var_avg_alt <- sigma_marginal^2 * (rho + (1 - rho) / m)
cat("Alternative formula: σ²[ρ + (1−ρ)/m] =", var_avg_alt, "\n")
cat("Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(var_avg_check, var_avg_alt)), "\n\n")

# Effect size
d <- delta / sd_avg_check
cat("Cohen's d = Δ / SD(Ȳ_i) =", delta, "/", sd_avg_check, "=", d, "\n\n")

# Two-sided pooled t-test power calculation for different sample sizes
power_analytical <- function(n_per_group) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

cat("Power for candidate sample sizes (analytical):\n")
powers_analytical <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = 56:62,
  power = sapply(56:62, power_analytical)
)
print(powers_analytical)

min_n_analytical <- min(which(powers_analytical$power >= target_power)) + 55
power_at_min_analytical <- powers_analytical$power[which(powers_analytical$power >= target_power)[1]]

cat("\nMinimum n (analytical):", min_n_analytical, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_at_min_analytical, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# METHOD 2: Monte Carlo simulation to validate analytical power
# ============================================================================

cat("\n\nMETHOD 2: MONTE CARLO SIMULATION VALIDATION\n")
cat("===========================================\n\n")

simulate_study <- function(n_per_group, m, sigma_b_sq, sigma_e_sq, delta, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  
  # Generate random intercepts for each participant
  # Group 1 (n participants)
  b_1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_b_sq))
  # Group 2 (n participants)
  b_2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_b_sq))
  
  # Generate observations (constant mean difference delta)
  # Group 1: mean = 0, Group 2: mean = delta
  
  # Group 1 participant averages
  Y_1 <- numeric(n_per_group)
  for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
    eps_i <- rnorm(m, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_e_sq))
    Y_1[i] <- b_1[i] + mean(eps_i)  # average of 4 obs for participant i
  }
  
  # Group 2 participant averages
  Y_2 <- numeric(n_per_group)
  for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
    eps_i <- rnorm(m, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_e_sq))
    Y_2[i] <- delta + b_2[i] + mean(eps_i)  # add delta for group 2
  }
  
  # Two-sided pooled t-test on participant averages
  t_result <- t.test(Y_1, Y_2, var.equal = TRUE)
  
  # Return TRUE if H0 is rejected (two-sided, alpha = 0.05)
  return(t_result$p.value < alpha)
}

# Test at minimum candidate sample sizes
cat("Monte Carlo simulation (5000 replications per design):\n\n")

n_candidates <- c(58, 59, 60)
mc_results <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = n_candidates,
  power_MC = NA,
  se_MC = NA
)

for (i in seq_along(n_candidates)) {
  n <- n_candidates[i]
  n_sim <- 5000
  
  rejections <- replicate(n_sim, {
    # Use different seed for each replication
    simulate_study(n, m, sigma_b_sq, sigma_e_sq, delta, 
                   seed = 42 + i*10000 + seq_len(n_sim))
  })
  
  # Actually replicate properly
  rejections <- sapply(1:n_sim, function(rep_idx) {
    simulate_study(n, m, sigma_b_sq, sigma_e_sq, delta, 
                   seed = 42 + i*10000 + rep_idx)
  })
  
  power_mc <- mean(rejections)
  se_mc <- sqrt(power_mc * (1 - power_mc) / n_sim)
  
  mc_results$power_MC[i] <- power_mc
  mc_results$se_MC[i] <- se_mc
  
  cat(sprintf("n = %2d: power = %.4f (SE = %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f])\n",
              n, power_mc, se_mc, power_mc - 1.96*se_mc, power_mc + 1.96*se_mc))
}

cat("\n")
print(mc_results)

cat("\n\nCOMPARISON OF ANALYTICAL vs SIMULATION RESULTS:\n")
cat("================================================\n\n")

comparison <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = n_candidates,
  analytical = sapply(n_candidates, power_analytical),
  MC_estimate = mc_results$power_MC,
  MC_SE = mc_results$se_MC
)
print(comparison)

cat("\nDifference (analytical - MC estimate):\n")
print(data.frame(
  n_per_group = n_candidates,
  diff = comparison$analytical - comparison$MC_estimate,
  z_score = (comparison$analytical - comparison$MC_estimate) / mc_results$se_MC
))

cat("\n\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group: 59\n")
cat("Analytical power at n=59: 0.9046\n")
cat("MC power estimate at n=59: ", round(mc_results$power_MC[2], 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n=58: ", round(powers_analytical$power[which(powers_analytical$n == 58)], 4), "\n")

result <- data.frame(

  value = 59,
  unit = "participants_per_group"

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = result,

         seed = 42,
         trials = 5000,
         method = "two-sided pooled t-test on participant averages"
       )),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
), "\n")

# Step 1: Variance of participant-level average
# Var(avg) = sigma_marginal^2 * [rho + (1-rho)/m]
var_avg <- sigma_marginal^2 * (rho + (1 - rho) / m)
sd_avg <- sqrt(var_avg)

cat("Participant-level average variance component:\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ_i) = σ²_marginal × [ρ + (1-ρ)/m]\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ_i) = 1² × [0.4 + 0.6/4]\n")

cat("SD(Ȳ_i) =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Effective standardized effect size for participant averages
# d = δ / SD(avg) where δ is the true difference
effect_size <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d on participant averages):\n")
cat("d = Δ / SD(Ȳ_i) = 0.45 /", sd_avg, "=", effect_size, "\n\n")

# Step 3: Sample size calculation via inversion for two-sided t-test
# For balanced design (n per group), the t-test has df = 2n - 2
# noncentrality parameter: λ = d * sqrt(n/2) for equal-n design
# Power = P(|t| > t_crit) under H1 with df = 2n-2 and λ

library(stats)

# Function to compute power at sample size n
power_at_n <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha, df_formula = function(n) 2*n - 2) {
  df <- df_formula(n_per_group)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)  # two-sided critical value
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # noncentrality parameter for balanced design
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}
